name: Shellfish gathering, Pinnacle Point, South Africa
summary: Middle Stone Age deposits at Pinnacle Point Cave 13B preserve evidence of shellfish gathering about 164,000 years ago.
description: The oldest shell-bearing layers reported at Pinnacle Point Cave 13B near Mossel Bay are dated to about 164,000 ± 12,000 years ago. Brown mussels are prominent in the assemblage. The excavation team inferred collection on rocky shores and in tidal pools based on the habitats of the shellfish.

impact.note: Shore foods extended foraging to a new and dependable food for people of one coast; wider consequences, such as coastal routes out of Africa, are suggested and not demonstrated in the sources read.

date.label: c. 164,000 years ago (±12,000)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The LC-MSA Lower at Pinnacle Point Cave 13B preserves an assemblage of marine shells interpreted as food remains, dated to about 164,000 ± 12,000 years ago.

evidence.supports: Reports luminescence dating of the lower deposit and identifies Perna perna as the most abundant shellfish by minimum number of individuals in that layer. Uses living shellfish habitats to infer intertidal collection.

earliest_record.rationale: The excavation report includes the dating uncertainty of the oldest shell-bearing deposits reviewed here.

unresolved.note: Daily and spring low tides both expose the inferred rocky shore and pools. Exactly when foragers collected remains unresolved.

evidence.supports: Reports luminescence dating of the lower deposit and identifies Perna perna as the most abundant shellfish by minimum number of individuals in that layer. Uses living shellfish habitats to infer intertidal collection.

unresolved.note: Bajondillo Cave independently records shellfish use around 150 ka. The locally reported age does not settle global priority.

evidence.supports: Reports separate shellfishing evidence at Bj19 roughly contemporaneous with Pinnacle Point.

unresolved.note: The coordinates are for the promontory and need checking against a gazetteer.

research.note: The Nature excavation paper and its press release describe the same dated observation. The version with dating uncertainty is retained.
